questions.question: How many times is the body of a do-while executed at minimum?
explanations: The do-while checks the condition AFTER, so the body runs at least 1 time.
Correct. do-while executes the body at least once regardless of the condition.
It is not always 2; it depends on the condition after the first iteration.
It is false: it always runs at least once.
It is not infinite: the body does not run because the condition is false.
Correct. 10 < 5 is false, the while does not enter, it only prints 'fin'.
It does not print 10 because the body does not run.
break would end the loop immediately, it is not the ideal solution.
Correct. You must increment i (i++) inside the body so the condition eventually becomes false.
Changing the operator does not prevent the infinite loop.
